00 · Start here
A growth breakdown for Lensa
Why we made this

Prisma Labs has been building AI photo apps since 2016, and Lensa's home page now leads with "Grow your Instagram. Create a feed worth following." The eraser and the enhancer are marked new, every tool is shown as a before and after, and your App Store listing promises "Natural, realistic edits", with 4.7 stars from 418K ratings.

This board is one idea for showing that every week: everyday creators in the US and UK taking one real photo from their camera roll and showing the same photo before and after, from Thanksgiving trips to New Year profile pictures. It is free, so take whatever is useful.

How to read this board
Use the list on the left, or press P to go frame by frame. On a phone, just scroll.
Creator cards: platform, followers and median views on recent videos.
Please note
Made by hypjam from public information, checked 2 Nov 2026. Nobody at Lensa asked for this, and it is not paid work. The creators named here have not been contacted and have no link to hypjam: they show the kind of people we would cast.
12 creators shortlisted, 4 scripts with 32 hooks, and a plan to put Lensa's eraser, enhancer and effects on real photos, from Thanksgiving trips to New Year profile pictures.
Four numbers to remember
418K: ratings on the US App Store, at 4.7 stars (read 2 Nov)
70M+: downloads of Lensa, from your home page
3.8M: plays on one creator's "How to Take Photos When You Travel Alone" (March 2025)
26 Nov: Thanksgiving, then holiday trips, December camera rolls and New Year profile photos
Who made this

hypjam is a UGC agency in London. We cast, script, direct and edit creators for consumer startups, and run the best videos as ads.

01 · Why UGC
Why creator videos work
Authenticity
People trust people
Your App Store page says Lensa keeps photos "true to life". A creator showing the same photo from their own trip, before and after, is the proof.
Show, do not tell
The slider is the demo
Your home page already shows every tool as a before and after. A short video does the same with a real camera roll, in the first second.
Objections
Answer "will it look edited?"
Every video changes the light, the background or the style of one photo. Viewers see for themselves that the person in it looks the same.
A real moment
December fills camera rolls
Thanksgiving trips, holiday lights and New Year's Eve all end up as photos people want to post that same week. Creators showing the edit on the day give them a reason to install Lensa then.
Fuel for ads
Creator videos become your ads
Each creator video doubles as a partnership ad. Eight openings per script means the budget goes where viewers actually stay.
Doesn't feel like an ad
Looks like a photo dump
So people watch it to the end instead of scrolling past. It is still labelled as an ad, it just does not interrupt.
02 · What we learned
Where Lensa is today
The product
Lensa AI: Photo Editor, by Prisma Labs: "Make every photo share-worthy." Trendy effects (Golden Hour, Halo Flash, Disposable and G7X), an eraser for photobombers, crowds, signs and power lines that rebuilds the background, an enhancer that upscales heavy crops and rescues bad lighting, Hair try-on, and presets that grade color, light and mood in a single tap. On iPhone, Mac and Android.
Just shipped
Marked new on lensa.app: the eraser ("Remove anything") and the enhancer ("Restore every detail"), on a home page that leads with "Grow your Instagram". 31 August to 29 September: three iPhone updates, versions 8.11.0, 8.12.0 and 8.13.0, for smoother performance.
Your numbers
4.7 stars from 418K ratings on the US App Store. 70M+ downloads of Lensa, from your home page, and 200M+ downloads across Prisma Labs apps since 2016, from prisma-ai.com. Prisma, your first app, was App of the Year on both the App Store and Google Play.
Already in motion
  • Your home page talks to people who post: "Turn everyday photos into scroll-stopping posts with the AI effects top creators swear by."
  • Every tool on the page is shown as a before and after, from Golden Hour to the eraser.
  • @lensa.ai on Instagram and @lensa on TikTok are linked from lensa.app.
What that tells us
Lensa is built for the moment between taking a photo and posting it, and your site already speaks to people who post. What is missing is volume: everyday creators showing one real photo, before and after, every week, in front of everyone with a full camera roll.
The timing
Thanksgiving is 26 November and Black Friday the day after. December brings trips, lights and parties, and the New Year is a natural moment to refresh a profile photo. Videos started in November have a month to find the hooks that work.
Sources: lensa.app (home, terms, privacy), prisma-ai.com (home, about, contacts), the US App Store listing and version history (version 8.13.0, 29 Sep 2026), Apple's public lookup API, the Google Play listing, and @lensa on TikTok, all read 2 Nov 2026.
03 · The category
What photo TikTok already films
Solo photos
Taking your own pictures is a genre
"How to Take Photos When You Travel Alone" passed 3.8M plays (March 2025), a Miami creator's guide to taking your own pictures 772K, and a Manchester creator's "how i take my photos" 182K.
Clean-up
Removing strangers already travels
A Dallas travel creator's "this is how I remove people from my photos when I'm traveling" passed 106K plays (October 2025).
Effects
The digicam look
A digicam-effect sunset video passed 1M plays from an account with 826 followers (July), and a G7X tripod photo session 686K (July). Camera looks are a whole corner of the feed.
Profile photos
Profile pictures get votes
A work-from-home headshot video passed 608K plays (March 2025), and a London creator's "I need your help choosing a new profile pic" for LinkedIn 42K in the last week.
City light
Golden hour, on repeat
"chasing sunsets in nyc" passed 1.5M plays on 24 October, and the same creator's favorite NYC photo spots 256K (August).
Also in play
Other photo and camera apps already pay creators for these videos: tutorials marked as paid partnerships turned up in most of our searches. The format is proven, and Lensa's before and afters are made for it.
The opening for Lensa
People already film how they take their photos. What these videos rarely show is the step after: the same photo with the crowd gone, the light back and one look applied. That is the Lensa moment, and the videos we would start with.
Sources: public TikTok search results for about 25 photo searches (taking your own photos, removing people, digicam effects, travel photo dumps, LinkedIn and dating profile photos, concert photos) and about 70 creator profiles, read through TikTok's public pages and embeds on 2 Nov 2026.
04 · The objection
"I don't want it to look edited": the objection to win
Most people worry an edited photo stops looking like them. The videos should answer with the same photo, side by side: the light, the background and the style change, and the person does not.
What you already say
  • Natural, realistic edits
  • Your pictures look their best while staying true to life
  • Erase unwanted objects and distractions so the focus stays on you
  • Transform any photo or video with filters and color tones
  • Simple, quick and fun, no skills required
Your own slider
lensa.app shows every tool as a before and after you can drag. In a video that is one shot: the creator's thumb dragging across their own photo.
One photo, one change
Every script changes one thing a viewer can name: the strangers, the dark, the color or the background. The creator says what changed, and the rest of the photo stays as it was.
How we use it
Script A removes the crowd from a trip photo. Script B brings back a dark photo. Script C tries four looks on one photo. Script D picks a profile picture, same face, better light.
Keep it honest
No face or body edits on camera, and no talk about faces or bodies. Before and after is always the same photo, and the creator's face stays their own.
What creators never say
No promises about likes, matches or job offers. Nothing your own pages do not say Lensa does. No children in any photo, including in the background.
05 · Audience
Who to sell to first
Start here
People who take their own photos
Tripod and self-timer creators who already film how they get the shot. The step after the shot is the product demo. Formats A and C.
Start here
Travelers with a full camera roll
Solo travelers and city explorers whose best photos have strangers, signs or dark corners in them. Formats A and B.
Broadest reach
Photo dump and feed people
Creators who post photo dumps and care how their grid looks. One photo in four looks is a video people save and comment on. Format C.
Next
Profile photo refreshers
People updating a LinkedIn or dating profile picture in the New Year, who want better light and a clean background, not a different face. Format D.
Where we would start
People who take their own photos first. Their videos already end where Lensa starts, the edit looks like the tutorials they post, and every viewer has a camera roll full of almost-right photos. Travel and photo dumps follow in December, profile photos in January.
06 · The moment
From Thanksgiving trips to New Year profile photos
Thanksgiving is 26 November, December fills every camera roll with trips and lights, and the New Year is when people refresh their profile photos. Videos filmed in November are tested before that rush.
Now to Thanksgiving (26 Nov)
6 to 8 creators who take their own photos film Script A on real trip photos. The first partnership ads go live on Meta and TikTok.
Black Friday (27 Nov) to the holidays
Photo dump creators film Script C, city and concert creators film Script B on dark evening photos, and budget moves to the hooks that win.
January
Profile photo refreshers film Script D for LinkedIn and dating profiles, while the best travel and photo dump videos keep running as ads.
What this needs from you
  • Full Lensa access for each creator, so every tool is on screen
  • A tracking link per creator to the App Store and Google Play
  • A short list of the tools creators may show, so videos only show what ships
  • One person on your team who signs off within 48 hours
Why not wait for January?
Holiday photos get edited and posted the same week they are taken. Videos filmed in November are tested and cut by December, so the budget backs proven hooks, not first drafts.
07 · The first month
Your first four weeks
Week 1 · 9-15 Nov
Shortlist and formats signed off. Creators get full Lensa access, a script with 8 hooks and a few days to edit their own photos before anyone films, so every before and after is theirs.
Week 2 · 16-22 Nov
The first eraser videos land and we review each one within 48 hours. They get 15 and 30 second ad cuts, and hook testing begins.
Week 3 · 23-29 Nov
Thanksgiving and Black Friday week. Budget follows the openings and creators that bring installs, and photo dump creators film their first four-looks videos.
Week 4 · 30 Nov-6 Dec
A results call: installs by creator and by ad, what to keep, and the plan for December photos and New Year profile pictures.
If it is a yes this week
Agreements signed and accounts out by Friday. The first videos go live within 14 days of script sign-off.
08 · Formats
Four formats for Lensa
A · Installs
Don't delete it, erase it
The creator opens a trip photo with strangers, a sign or power lines behind them, brushes over them in Lensa, and shows the same photo before and after. Then it goes in the photo dump. Cut into 15 and 30 second partnership ads.
removing people from travel photos, 106K ↗the eraser on your home page ↗
B · Installs
The photo I almost deleted
A photo taken in a dark room or cropped in tight: a concert, a dinner, the city at night. The enhancer brings back the light and the detail, and the creator shows both versions side by side.
the enhancer on your home page ↗a first concert in Tampa, 450K ↗
C · Reach
One photo, four looks
One photo, four effects: Golden Hour, Halo Flash, Disposable and G7X, then one preset for the whole photo dump. The creator picks a favorite and asks the comments which one they would post.
a G7X tripod photo session, 686K ↗chasing sunsets in NYC, 1.5M ↗
D · Saves
Profile photo day
The creator takes their own profile photo at home or outside, then brings back the light, clears the background and picks a preset in Lensa. Same face, same person, a better photo for LinkedIn or a dating app.
a work-from-home headshot, 608K ↗"help me choose a new profile pic", 42K ↗
In every video
1 One real photo from the creator's own camera roll. 2 Lensa on screen in the first 5 seconds. 3 The same photo before and after, side by side. 4 Only the light, the background, distractions and the style change, never a face or a body. 5 "Ad | Paid partnership with Lensa" on screen plus the platform label.

Takeaway
Photo how-tos, clean-ups and camera looks travel far past their creators' follower counts. So we would run many everyday creators side by side, testing 8 hooks per script.
Where the market is
Your home page already speaks to people who post, with a before and after for every tool. Everyday creators showing those before and afters on their own photos are the next pool of faces, and the closest to the people scrolling with a full camera roll.
10 · Script A
Script A: Don't delete it, erase it
The brief

Where: TikTok and Instagram Reels from the creator's account, plus 15s and 30s Meta and TikTok partnership ads pointing at the App Store and Google Play

Length: 25-30s master. 30s cut: shots 1 to 5 and 7. 15s cut: shots 1, 2, 4 and 7 (hook, disclosure, the erase, CTA).

Goal: Installs of Lensa on iPhone and Android

Who films it: A US or UK creator, 18+, who travels and takes their own photos. They use Lensa on their own photos for a few days first. Phone on a tripod or in hand, plus a screen recording of Lensa. The trip photo has no children in it, in front or behind.

8 hooks to test (on screen, then spoken)
  1. Don't delete it. Erase it.Don't delete the photo. Just erase the crowd.
  2. The best photo of my trip had a crowd in itThe best photo of my whole trip had a crowd in it.
  3. Perfect photo. One photobomber.Perfect photo, except for one photobomber.
  4. Watch the power lines disappearWatch these power lines disappear.
  5. Same photo. No crowd.Same photo. No crowd.
  6. I brushed over the sign. Gone.I just brushed over that sign, and it's gone.
  7. Nobody had to move for this photoNobody had to move for this photo.
  8. Day [X] of my trip: cleaning up the camera rollDay [X] of my trip, and I'm cleaning up the camera roll.
Shot list
TimeWhat we seeOn screenSpoken
0-2sThe trip photo full screen: the creator in front of a landmark, strangers, a sign or power lines behind them.[Hook on-screen text] + 'Ad | Paid partnership with Lensa' label top-left for the whole video[Hook spoken line]
2-5sCreator to camera, phone in hand.Ad | Paid partnership with LensaQuick heads up, Lensa is paying me for this one. Watch.

Lensa named at 0:02 in the spoken disclosure and on screen by 0:05 (the photo opened in Lensa). Hero moment 0:09-0:20: the brush stroke, then the same photo before and after. The 15s cut keeps the erase.

CTA: Install Lensa from the App Store or Google Play ([offer as on posting day]). In the ad cuts the button goes straight to the store.

Rules for this video

FTC: 'Ad | Paid partnership with Lensa' on screen from 0s to the end, said out loud by 0:05, the platform's paid-partnership label switched on (TikTok content disclosure, Instagram and Facebook 'Paid partnership'), and the caption opens with the disclosure. Partnership ads run from the creator's own handle. Honest edits: the before and after is always the same photo, exported exactly as Lensa made it. Only light, background, distractions and style change; no face or body tools, and no talk about faces or bodies. No children anywhere in any photo, including strangers in the background before an erase. No alcohol in any photo. No promises about likes, matches or job offers. Only claims from lensa.app and the App Store listing: the eraser removes photobombers, crowds, signs, power lines and large objects and rebuilds the background; natural, realistic edits; no skills required. Plan and offer details exactly as on the posting day.

Why it should convert
It is the clearest before and after Lensa has: one brush stroke, one photo saved. Everyone has a trip photo with a stranger in it, so the hook lands in a second, and the result looks like the photo dumps these creators already post.

The brief

Where: TikTok and Instagram Reels from the creator's account, plus 15s and 30s Meta and TikTok partnership ads pointing at the App Store and Google Play

Product moment and call to action

Lensa named at 0:02 and on screen by 0:05. Hero moment 0:10-0:26: better light, a clean background, one preset, three honest options next to their originals. The 15s cut keeps the edit.

Caption
Ad | Paid partnership with Lensa (@lensa on TikTok, @lensa.ai on Instagram). Profile photo day: same face, better light. Which one would you pick? #ad #lensa #linkedinphoto #profilepicture
Rules for this video

FTC: 'Ad | Paid partnership with Lensa' on screen from 0s to the end, said out loud by 0:05, the platform's paid-partnership label switched on (TikTok content disclosure, Instagram and Facebook 'Paid partnership'), and the caption opens with the disclosure. Partnership ads run from the creator's own handle. Honest edits: the before and after is always the same photo, exported exactly as Lensa made it. Only light, background, distractions and style change; no face or body tools, and no talk about faces or bodies. No children anywhere in any photo, including strangers in the background before an erase. No alcohol in any photo. No promises about likes, matches or job offers. This script uses no face or body tools: the creator's face and body are shown exactly as photographed, and the creator says so on camera. Only claims from lensa.app and the App Store listing: the enhancer rescues bad lighting; the eraser removes unwanted objects and distractions so the focus stays on you; presets grade color, light and mood; natural, realistic edits; no skills, no studio. Plan and offer details exactly as on the posting day.

Why it should convert
Everyone needs a profile photo and few people have a photographer. Voting on three honest options brings comments, and it shows the eraser, the enhancer and presets on the photo people care about most: the one with their own face, left as it is.

16 · Ads
How the paid ads would run
1 · Film
Each script is shot once, with 8 different openings.
→
2 · Launch
Each opening runs as its own ad, from the creator's handle as a partnership ad.
→
3 · Read
After a few days we compare cost per install and how many people watch past 3 seconds.
4 · Cut
The weakest openings switch off and the budget moves to the best two.
→
5 · Remix
Winning hooks get new bodies and new creators.
→
6 · Refresh
New creator videos every week, so the ads never go stale.
Where the ads point
Your App Store and Google Play listings, with one tracking link per creator, so every install traces back to the video that drove it.
Why partnership ads
Ads that run from a creator's own handle look like that creator's post, not a brand ad. That is the format these videos are built for.
What we would need
Each creator's OK for partnership ads, access to your Meta and TikTok ad accounts (or ad sets we run next to your team), and a weekly look at installs and subscription starts.
17 · Process
How a campaign runs, step by step
1 · Brief
You tell us the goal, the audience and what can and can't be said about Lensa.
→
2 · Cast
We shortlist creators by niche, location and median views. You pick.
→
3 · Offer
We send each creator the brief, the dates and the rate.
4 · Sign
A written agreement with every creator, covering usage and disclosure.
→
5 · Scripts
One per format: 8 hooks, a shot list, screens to record and a caption.
→
6 · Film and upload
Creators film on their phones and upload to a private folder only we see.
7 · Review
We check every video within 48 hours. Nothing posts unapproved.
→
8 · Post
On the creator's own account, with the ad disclosure and the paid-partnership label.
→
9 · Pay and report
Creators paid within 7 days of going live. You get a report every Monday.
Where creators talk to us
One hypjam Discord for every creator. Each campaign gets a private channel group for chat, scripts and posted links that only its creators and your team can see.
Accounts and real photos
Each signed creator gets full Lensa access from you and edits their own photos for a few days before filming, so every before and after is theirs. We agree which photos and tools each video shows before anyone records.
18 · Reporting
What we report, and when
Every video
Views, how many people stay past 3 seconds, average watch time, saves, shares and comments.
Every creator link
A tracking link for each creator, so installs trace back to the video that drove them.
Every Monday
A short report: every video, the hooks that won, installs by creator, and what we change next.
Every month
A review call: spend, installs, cost per result on anything run as an ad, and the plan for next month.
19 · Rules
Rules we never break
Disclosure
"Ad | Paid partnership with Lensa" on screen, said in the first seconds, and the platform's paid-partnership label on. That is what the FTC asks for.
Who films
Adults only (18+). Creators use Lensa themselves before they talk about it.
What gets said
Nothing your own pages do not say Lensa does. No invented numbers. We never pay for a positive opinion, only for the video.
Honest edits
Before and after is always the same photo, shown the way Lensa edited it. Videos change light, background, distractions and style, never a face or a body. No talk about faces or bodies, and no promises about likes, matches or job offers.
Adults only, in every photo
Every creator is 18+, and so is everyone in every photo they show, including strangers in the background before an erase. Anyone recognisable who stays in a photo has agreed to be in it.
How we run it
Every video reviewed within 48 hours before it posts. Creators paid within 7 days of going live.
